about: How long a token lives (ADR 0020, "Lifetimes"; REQ-TOKEN-036, REQ-TOKEN-037, REQ-TOKEN-049; the resource caps are REQ-TOKEN-051, planned for #791). A token lives for the shortest of the built-in maximum (3600 seconds), the issuer's lifetime for its type (TokenLifetime.id_token or .access_token), the audience's caps (the client's ttl_cap, and the resource's ttl_cap when a request names a resource) and never past the end of the session chain that backs it or of the proof that was exchanged. Every limit only shortens: a cap above the issuer's lifetime changes nothing. A limit that is left out, zero or negative is not set. All durations are whole seconds; chain_left and proof_left are the seconds from now to the end (zero or negative: already over). now_fraction_ms is how far into a second now is, because a token writes iat and exp in whole seconds and never lives past the end by rounding. lifetime is exp minus iat; refused says no token is issued (less than a second left). cap is what signer holds exp minus iat to for the type and the audience, whatever the chain or the proof says, so it ignores chain_left and proof_left. The ID token and the access token are the same rule with their own issuer lifetime. kits/go/lifetime, session and exchange are held to lifetime; actors/signer is held to cap. v1 keeps the same rule: the lifetime of the deployment, narrowed by the client's ttl_cap, and the shorter of the client's and the resource's caps wins; v2 has no resource yet, so a resource_ttl_cap vector is the rule that resources will use.
